rules: The title plan and register record the general position of registered boundaries unless a boundary is shown as determined exactly.
An index polygon forms part of the statutory Index and indicates the location of a registered title.
National Polygon index polygons are held in vector format.
The title plan and register share the title number as their identifier.
Every registered title has at least one index polygon.
Each index polygon has a unique Polygon ID.
National Polygon, Title Descriptor and UPRN data are separated to make the datasets smaller and easier to manage and maintain.
INSPIRE Index Polygons are a subset of National Polygon data with identifier, creation-date and last-update attributes.
An index-polygon extent may be the same size, larger or smaller than the title-plan extent and must not be relied on as exact.
HMLR completed conversion of 19 million paper index polygons to vector polygons in February 2004.
HMLR's Positional Accuracy Improvement programme ran from 2005 to 2008.
Almost 14 million index polygons passed through the Quality Improvement Flowline initiative.
Daily OS MasterMap change-only updates support new polygons and title plans rather than routine updating of current registrations.
Referenced large-scale OS mapping uses 1:1,250 urban, 1:2,500 semi-urban/rural and 1:10,000 mountain/moorland scales.
HMLR index polygons are captured in British National Grid.
Publication processing checks zero-coordinate polygons, zero-area polygons and duplicate coordinate points.
Many self-intersections are cleaned and polygons below 0.1 square metres are removed from the publication environment.
National Polygon validation files follow the LR_POLY_VALI_<month> naming pattern.
Title plans and index polygons are not routinely updated; specified customer, adjoining-title, error or land-sale activity can trigger changes.

The 1m LIDAR Composite DTM covers approximately 99 percent of England.
The DTM is produced from the last or only laser pulse returned to the sensor.
Surface objects are removed from the DSM using bespoke algorithms and manual editing to produce bare terrain.
The composite DTM was produced by the Environment Agency in 2022.
The composite combines Time Stamped archive surveys with National LIDAR Programme surveys.
Where surveys repeat, the newest best-resolution data is selected.
Bilinear interpolation is used where source data is resampled before merging.
The 2022 composite includes surveys from 6 June 2000 through 2 April 2022.
Individual source surveys can have spatial resolutions between 25 centimetres and 2 metres.
The published vertical accuracy is plus or minus 15 centimetres RMSE.
The published coordinate reference system is EPSG:27700.
The dataset record gives a creation date of 8 February 2023.
The dataset record gives a revision date of 15 December 2023.
The official record lists WMS, WCS, WMTS and OGC API Features access surfaces.

OS Terrain 50 is Open Data and is free for commercial, educational and personal use.
The grid GML file provides location, grid-spacing, vertical-reference and spatial-reference metadata for the ASCII data.
Each grid tile supply contains an Esri ASCII grid file named from the tile reference.
Each grid tile supply contains a GML file that enables loading the ASCII grid as GML.
Each grid tile supply contains a PRJ file describing the spatial reference system.
Each grid tile supply contains an asc.aux.xml file for default Esri styling parameters.
Each grid tile supply contains a per-tile XML metadata file including flying-date information.
Raster construction creates no tile overlaps and no common height values along tile edges.
Mean high and low water heights are assigned from a per-tile average based on local tide tables.
Mean high and low water lines are used as heighted breaklines to keep grid and contour products consistent.
The Esri auxiliary XML supplies min, max, mean and standard-deviation height statistics intended to style adjacent tiles consistently.
